question: Should `tool-progress` become a permanent public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract for bundled and third-party plugins?
rationale: A generic seam is architecturally plausible because Codex and Slack cannot import each other’s private implementation, but permanent public API direction requires maintainer ownership rather than reviewer inference.

options.title: Keep the generic contract
options.body: Retain the additive kind and predicate as the canonical cross-plugin progress intent, repair every Slack representation, and lock the contract with focused tests.

options.title: Use a private core seam
options.body: Carry the same typed intent through an internal reply contract without exporting a new third-party Plugin SDK API.

options.title: Narrow to Slack inference
options.body: Drop producer typing and use a Slack-local classifier only if maintainers explicitly accept the ambiguity and maintenance drift.

recommendation.title: Keep the generic contract
recommendation.body: Retain the additive kind and predicate as the canonical cross-plugin progress intent, repair every Slack representation, and lock the contract with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership across the native Slack block-delivery surface and adjacent reply-payload behavior.
